sections.title: Using a multimeter
sections.summary: Volts across, amps through, and what each reading tells you

blocks.text: Volts are measured **across**: one probe on each side of the part, circuit left alone. Amps are measured **through**: break the loop and put the meter in the gap.

items: Volts: dial to V (DC is the straight-line symbol), black lead in COM, red in V.
Touch black to ground or one side of the part, red to the other. A minus sign means red is lower than black.
Amps: dial to A or mA, black in COM, red moved to the A or mA socket.
Break the loop (lift a wire, open a link) and put the probes in the gap, so the current goes through the meter.
Move the red lead back to V when you're done. A meter left in amps and put across a battery shorts it and blows its fuse.
